name: is_pinned
description: Representative ATen schema (verbatim): aten::is_pinned(Tensor self, Device? device=None) -> bool. This is a representative overload, not an exclusive ABI: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and tests must never be narrowed, deleted or have reference behavior adapted to fit this single signature. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: ["aten::is_pinned(Tensor self, Device? device=None) -> bool"]. Semantics from the tests: is_pinned is a storage/allocator query with no elementwise result, no gradient and no broadcast form; it returns a Python bool (type checked with type(res_out) is bool and compared by identity to torch.ops.aten.is_pinned). A tensor backed by page-locked host storage (CPU pin_memory=True, including flat, non-contiguous view, zero-dim and special-payload allocations) reports True, while plain host storage, backend/device-resident storage, meta storage and zero-element empty storage report False. Views (transpose, narrow, step-slice, expand, as_strided-offset, select, diagonal, detach, unsqueeze) report the pinning of the storage they were taken from (asserted True for a pinned base) and still share that base storage/data_ptr after the query; newly allocated storage (clone, contiguous-of-transpose, empty-like, to-backend) never inherits page locking and reports False. The optional device argument is exercised by omission, explicit None, torch.device objects and device strings, passed both positionally and by keyword, with pinned-host plus a CPU device (or explicit CPU string) reporting False and pinned-host plus the backend device reporting True; an explicit None or omission leaves the outcome unchanged. Invalid inputs raise RuntimeError or TypeError: non-tensor self (list, int, None, str), a missing self, and invalid device values (int, float, unrecognized string). Empty (zero-element) storage is a separate case and is expected not to be pinned even when allocated with pin_memory=True. The conjugate view of a pinned complex storage keeps the lazy conj bit and its base storage but has no hard-coded pinning literal: the test defers to the measured native answer (this build reports False for that view). Only the representative overload's effects are modeled here; overload-dependent or condition-dependent behavior remains the business of the original pytest.
